How these candidates work

Hit frequency: Ordinary shots make an accuracy check against effective skill. Passing puts the shot in a central cluster, using one quarter of the sampled angular error. Failing preserves the original scatter. This makes hits more frequent without narrowing failed shots. A passed check can still miss or hit cover; critical events override the check.

Angular scatter: Skill, aim and weapon precision set an error angle. A random rotation places that error around the muzzle-to-aim axis. Offset at the target is distance × tan(error). Apparent target width is 2 × atan(width ÷ (2 × distance)). No extra distance penalty or close-range placement floor.

Angular + D20: Natural 20 (5%) aims exactly at the chosen point. Natural 1 (5%) produces a 28–48° error in a random direction. Rolls 2–19 use ordinary angular scatter. Collision always wins: perfect aim can hit cover; a wild shot can accidentally hit a body.

D20 roll + skill: The same critical events. Other rolls add floor((effective skill − 50) ÷ 10), then compare with a tuning target of 11. The margin sets angular spread; it never directly awards a hit. Aim adds 0 / 10 / 20 skill at 4 / 6 / 8 AP for this sample weapon.

Smoke caps damage only when a body hit passes through the smoke curtain. The optional bypass lifts that cap. Sample full damage is 45–55, with head ×1.5 and legs ×0.85; armor and resistance are omitted. Critical success means precise aim, not bonus damage. Damage per AP includes misses and blocked shots.

Prototype limits: Ellipsoid body proxies, static target, no animal meshes, held weapons, travel animation, visibility restrictions or live combat integration. These are uncalibrated game-balance candidates. Percentages are seeded sample estimates, not guaranteed chances. The angular reference intentionally has no D20 exceptions. Uniform random rotation means the helicoid twist does not change aggregate spread.
